I also reworked the Property and Signal handling. I still need to tidy up this PR and look into some missing topics: - [x] Also handle `InvokeGodotClassStaticMethod` - [ ] ~~Properties indexer support~~ - [x] Smallish tidy-up tasks After that this PR should be ready to be reviewed. ✨ Sneek peek The performance on **test_mono_method_cache** even increased and the process time is pretty much flat-lined (test_mono_method_cache and GodotSharp compiled with `true`): **2250FPS/1.1ms** ------ EDIT: I just realized I forgot that I did a fix on test_mono_method_cache because the random initialization didn't match the GD script (using `ints` instead of `doubles`, so replacing `GD.RandRange(1, 5)` with `GD.RandRange(1.0, 5.0)`). The original (mismatching) code now performs like this (C# enabled): 2550 FPS/9.9ms But still, comparing the fixed (=functionally equivalent) C# version with GD version makes C# still faster (more FPS, less ms)! GD version: 1879FPS/1.7ms

@AThousandShips It's ready for review now. I've tested with all the benchmark projects that were mentioned in the related tickets (PerformanceTestMRP_Godot4.5, test_mono_method_cache, HighNodeCountNoDeadCode) and also some more complex Godot projects (eg. https://catlikecoding.com/godot/introduction/5-migrating-to-c-sharp/ where there is some mixing of GD Script and C#). All seems to work the same way as before - just faster! 🚀

### Notes for Reviewers
* I exposed the _value_ of `StringName._data` and `godot_string_name._data` via internal `GetIntPtr()` as this is used for fast v-table like lookups - is that OK?
* The main reason for the speed improvement is the quasi v-table alias `ScriptCache`
* I added `scoped` and `in` keywords to a number of places related to the interop. This allows the compiler to more aggressively optimize parameter handling (eg. because the parameter is guaranteed to not escape the method)
* It very well be that the changes in `bindings_generator.cpp` could be written in a better way - I'm open for feedback/help.
* I strived to make the generated code readable, but I have 2 variants of registering dispatch methods: inline and in a separate class (`ScriptMethodDispatchHelper`). Can it stay as-is or should I change for 1 style (and which)?
* I tested it manually, but please also run the code locally with your own projects. Tip: Add `<Optimize>true</Optimize>` to `GodotSharp` and your test game project, then you see the full speed!
* As far as I see, C# indexers (eg. `this[string key]`) are not supported anyway in C# interop right now - am I right?

### Advertisment
As this is one of 2 PRs that tries to fix the issue, I want to bring it's benefits to your attention (and because it was a lot of work with many sleep deprived nights 😅).

This PR is entirely done in C# (except for `bindings_generator.cpp`). This allowed me to move, experiment and validate quickly. Having to compile the whole editor to see changes of the C++ source generation was already painfully slow. On the C# side, the only real painful thing was also writing the source generators - but with a much faster feedback loop! Other than that, it was a bliss as I as a C# developer could work with the tools and environment I already know.

A C# module can be maintained and improved much easier, if the target audience - C# developers - can understand and tune the code. Also this makes good patches more likely. Although I had some background in C++, I would have been lost trying to implement what I did in C++.

This PR shows that with modern C# only, you can really get to interop-speeds that exceed all expectations and are pretty much at the physical limits of interop. All without any change to the native code.

Thanks for considering this PR and I'm waiting for your feedback!

```
       [2] bool Godot.Bridge.CSharpInstanceBridge.Invoke(Godot.GodotObject, Godot.NativeInterop.godot_string_name*&, Godot.NativeInterop.godot_variant**&, int, Godot.NativeInterop.godot_variant_call_error*&, Godot.NativeInterop.godot_variant&)

```

I assume this is happening in an RPC call, but I'm not getting a stack trace for it. I tried removing all array RPCs, but I think that any RPC ends up as a Variant[] anyway, regardless of how it is invoked from C#.

Thank you @Seb105 !
With your reproduction sample I was able to analyze the problem. Please check again, it should work now.

In the end, the solution was easy: Don't care about the methods of the C# wrappers for Godot C++ entities, just register their aliases for later game-dev overrides.

This means, C++ code does not resolve eg. C#'s `EmitSignal(...)` and go C++ -> C# -> C++ - an unnecessary detour. Now it's executing the call in C++: C++ -> C++, no C# interop involved.

New binaries released here:
https://github.com/warappa/godot/releases/tag/4.7-dev-csharp-interop-optimization-2

@Seb105 Thank you again! With your repo I found the issue:
This branch needs a backwards-compatability path for NuGet packages that are built _without_ the source generators of this branch. Therefore no method registry is built for the NuGet class and for that reason the overridden C# methods like `_Ready()` inside the **_NuGet package's_** code are not "seen". In Seb's example the `GDTask` NuGet package.
